title: 24. Multi-Tenancy, vCluster & Crossplane
summary: Build enterprise-scale internal developer platforms using hard multi-tenancy (ResourceQuotas, LimitRanges, vCluster virtual clusters) and universal cloud control planes with Crossplane.
learningObjectives: Enforce strict compute, memory, and storage boundaries with ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges
Deploy and manage lightweight virtual Kubernetes clusters (vCluster) inside single namespaces
Define Crossplane Composite Resource Definitions (XRD) and Compositions for self-service cloud infrastructure
Decouple developer APIs from underlying cloud provider implementations

curriculumModules.title: Hard Multi-Tenancy & Virtual Clusters (vCluster)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Namespaces provide soft multi-tenancy. vCluster creates dedicated virtual control planes (API Server, Controller Manager, storage) inside host namespaces, giving tenants full cluster-admin rights without security compromises.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Multi-tenant developer environments where each engineering squad owns an isolated vCluster with dedicated CRDs.

curriculumModules.title: Crossplane: The Universal Cloud Control Plane
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Crossplane extends the Kubernetes API to manage any cloud or on-prem resource. Through XRDs and Compositions, platform teams publish simplified abstractions (e.g. PostgresInstance) that developers consume via GitOps.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Internal Developer Platform (IDP) vending self-service AWS RDS, Azure SQL, and GCP CloudSQL through standard Kubernetes claims.

labs.title: Hard Multi-Tenancy with ResourceQuota, LimitRange & vCluster
labs.scenario: A new product engineering team requires dedicated compute quotas and an isolated virtual cluster. Deploy a ResourceQuota, LimitRange, and spin up a vCluster for tenant-alpha.
labs.productionContext: ResourceQuotas prevent a single rogue tenant or memory leak from starving cluster-wide resources.
objectives: Create namespace tenant-alpha with a ResourceQuota capping CPU to 4 and memory to 8Gi
Create a LimitRange establishing default container requests and limits
Provision a virtual cluster using vcluster create tenant-alpha
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-alpha
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: compute-quota
  namespace: tenant-alpha
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    pods: "20"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-limits
  namespace: tenant-alpha
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      default:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 512Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi

steps.title: Apply Multi-Tenant Quotas & Limits
steps.instruction: Deploy the Namespace, ResourceQuota, and LimitRange from the Manifest Editor.

steps.title: Provision Virtual Cluster
steps.instruction: Create the tenant-alpha virtual cluster using the vcluster CLI.

validationRules.description: ResourceQuota compute-quota exists in tenant-alpha with 20 max pods
validationRules.name: compute-quota
validationRules.remediation: Deploy ResourceQuota compute-quota in tenant-alpha with spec.hard.pods: '20'.

validationRules.description: vcluster create command was executed for tenant-alpha
validationRules.remediation: Execute 'vcluster create tenant-alpha' in the terminal.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Confirm that pods: '20' is set in the ResourceQuota spec.hard map.

labs.title: Crossplane Composite Resource Platform Provisioning
labs.scenario: As a Platform Engineer, publish an enterprise PostgreSQL claim abstraction. Deploy a Crossplane PostgresInstance composite resource claim and verify its automated infrastructure provisioning.
labs.productionContext: Crossplane transforms Kubernetes into a control plane for multi-cloud infrastructure, eliminating custom Terraform wrapper scripts.
objectives: Deploy a PostgresInstance custom claim named fintech-payment-db
Configure storage to 50Gi and high availability parameters
Verify status and trace the composition using crossplane beta trace
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: database.platform.kubelabs.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostgresInstance
metadata:
  name: fintech-payment-db
  namespace: production
spec:
  parameters:
    storageGB: 50
    engineVersion: "16.2"
    highAvailability: true
  compositionSelector:
    matchLabels:
      provider: aws-rds

steps.title: Review Crossplane Claim Manifest
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor to inspect the PostgresInstance claim.

steps.title: Deploy PostgresInstance Claim
steps.instruction: Apply the claim to the production namespace.

steps.title: Trace Crossplane Provisioning
steps.instruction: Run crossplane beta trace to verify managed infrastructure reconciliation.

validationRules.name: fintech-payment-db
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create PostgresInstance fintech-payment-db.

validationRules.name: fintech-payment-db
validationRules.remediation: Ensure spec.parameters.highAvailability is set to true in the manifest.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Confirm that provider is set to 'aws-rds' in the compositionSelector.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary architectural difference between a Kubernetes namespace and a vCluster?
options: Namespaces share the host API server and etcd; vCluster provides an isolated virtual control plane with its own API server and CRDs inside a namespace
Namespaces require dedicated physical hardware; vCluster is pure software
vCluster only runs on bare-metal servers
assessmentQuestions.explanation: vCluster creates an in-cluster virtual control plane that gives tenants independent API servers and custom resources without cluster-admin risk on the host.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Crossplane architecture, what is the role of a Composite Resource Definition (XRD)?
options: It defines the custom API schema and type for an abstracted platform service (e.g. DatabaseInstance)
It replaces the Linux kernel on worker nodes
It backs up logs to tape storage
assessmentQuestions.explanation: An XRD defines the declarative OpenAPI schema for a composite resource that developers consume as a simplified cloud abstraction.
